Label the nine points as a \(3\times3\) grid:

\[
\begin{matrix}
A&B&C\\
D&E&F\\
G&H&I
\end{matrix}
\]

1. **Lower bound:** Each of the three horizontal rows \(ABC\), \(DEF\), and \(GHI\) contains three collinear points. At least one point must be removed from each row. Since the rows are disjoint, at least \(3\) points must be removed.

2. **Construction:** Remove \(A,E,I\), the three points on the main diagonal. Then:
   - every row and every column contains only two remaining points;
   - the other diagonal contains only \(C\) and \(G\), since \(E\) was removed;
   - no other line can contain three points of a \(3\times3\) grid.

Thus three removals are both necessary and sufficient.

\[
\boxed{3}
\]
